text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The edit preserves every existing function (routes_between, best_route, sites_served, trips_needed, CAPACITY, DEFAULT_VEHICLE) unchanged and only adds the two new functions. passable_route matches the ticket: it uses routes_between, tests each road via can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network) (signature matches logistics/access.py), treats a route as usable if truck or van can use every road, picks the shortest usable route with the same (km, id) ordering as best_route, and returns truck only if a truck can use every road on that route, else van, or None. rerouted_sites iterates warehouses and sites_served (sorted, so name order), compares route ids between passable_route and best_route so a vehicle-only change does not count, and skips sites where passable_route finds nothing. Verified against data/network.json: SITE-NVL-B (RT-02 van-only but same route as best) is correctly excluded; SITE-CPL-B (RT-06 vs RT-05) and SITE-HGL-A (RT-08 vs RT-07) are correctly included; SITE-HGL-B (RT-09 van-only, only route) is correctly excluded."}}
reasoning:
Check the proposed edit against the code.

passable_route: iterates routes_between, for each route checks vehicles in ("truck","van"), appends (route, vehicle) if all roads passable. Then picks min by (km, id). Then checks truck on all roads of that route; returns truck if yes else van. This matches the plan. Note: the vehicle picked in the loop is discarded and re-derived — fine.

Edge: a route usable only by van — appended with van. min picks shortest usable. Then truck check fails → van. Correct.

rerouted_sites: iterates warehouses sorted, sites_served sorted. For each site, passable_route vs best_route; include when found is None? No — skips when found is None. Hmm: ticket says rerouted_sites returns sites for which passable_route finds a route different from best_route. If passable_route returns None (no usable route), the site is not included — matches ticket ("for which passable_route finds a route that is different"). If best is None but found is not None — can that happen? best_route returns None only if no routes exist; passable_route would also return None then. So best is never None when found is not None. The check `best is None or found[0]["id"] != best[0]["id"]` is fine.

Wait — one subtlety: if found is None (no usable route), the site is skipped. Ticket: "the sites ... for which passable_route finds a route that is different from the route best_route picks". If passable_route finds nothing, it doesn't find a different route, so skipping is correct per ticket. Though arguably a site with no usable route is affected, the ticket's definition is explicit. OK.

Check data: SITE-NVL-B: RT-02 (R-01 A, R-03 R) — truck can't use R-03, van can → usable with van, km 22. RT-03 (R-04, R-05 both A) → truck, km 31. min usable = RT-02 (22) → truck check fails → van. best_route picks RT-02 (22 < 31). So route same, vehicle changes van — rerouted_sites should NOT include SITE-NVL-B. The code compares ids: RT-02 == RT-02 → not included. Correct.

SITE-CPL-B: RT-05 has R-08 X → not usable. RT-06 (R-07 A, R-09 R) → van only, km 26. best_route picks RT-05 (18). Different → included. Correct.

SITE-HGL-A: RT-07 has R-12 X → not usable. RT-08 (R-10, R-11 A) → truck, km 27. best picks RT-07 (20). Different → included. Correct.

SITE-HGL-B: RT-09 R-13 R → van only. best_route picks RT-09 too (only route). Same route → not included. Correct per ticket (vehicle-only change doesn't count).

SITE-NVL-A: RT-01 all A → truck, same as best. Not included. SITE-CPL-A: same. Correct.

Also check best_route unchanged: yes, identical. Other functions preserved: routes_between, sites_served, trips_needed, CAPACITY, DEFAULT_VEHICLE — all present. Import adds can_pass — exists in logistics/access.py with signature can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network=None). Good.

One thing: passable_route's docstring/type hints fine. The min over usable picks shortest usable route — but ticket says "passable_route returns (route, vehicle) for the shortest usable route, sending a truck if a truck may use every road on that route and a van otherwise". Yes.

Potential issue: in passable_route, the loop breaks after first usable vehicle — truck checked first, so vehicle recorded is truck if possible. But then it's discarded and re-derived. Fine.

Also check notifications/sms.py? Not needed for this edit. The edit only touches routes.py.

One more check: does anything else import from logistics.routes that could break? The edit keeps all existing functions with same signatures. Fine.

Verdict: accept.
